name: Loretto Academy
notes: IDENTITY PROBABLE BUT ZIP/ADDRESS WRONG: the best-documented 'Loretto Academy' in the St. Louis area was the Sisters of Loretto girls' academy at 3407 Lafayette Ave in St. Louis CITY (ZIP 63104) -- NRHP-listed building (NRIS 92000079, significant year 1909, architects Barnett Haynes & Barnett / John Costello). Per a St. Louis Post-Dispatch article quoted by UrbanReview STL, the building 'opened in 1907 as the Loretto Academy, a posh school for girls'; Nerinx Hall's own LibGuide dates 'Loretto Academy (St. Louis, MO)' as closed 1952, when the school moved to/merged with Nerinx Hall High School in Webster Groves (successor, no seed row). Nothing ties a 'Loretto Academy' to ZIP 63114 (Overland/St. Ann/Breckenridge Hills); the Sisters of Loretto school actually in that area was St. Ann parish school in Normandy, a different entity. ALTERNATIVE REFERENT: Loretto Academy in Florissant, MO -- a five-story Sisters of Loretto academy built 1882, destroyed by fire 1919 (city of Florissant historic marker, florissantmo.com). If the seed meant the Florissant school, the dates would be 1882-1919 instead. Recorded here as the city school (1907-1952); flag for human review.

name: Ritenour Adult Education
historical_names: Ritenour Adult Education and Learning (AEL) Program
notes: Still operating: per a Ritenour School District notice, the Adult Education and Learning (AEL) program moved July 1, 2025 from leased space at 8672 St. Charles Rock Rd (St. John) into the north wing of Hoech Middle School, 3312 Ashby Rd, for the 2025-26 year. SEED ADDRESS IS WRONG/IMPRECISE: 2420 Woodson Rd is the district Administrative Center, not the program's classroom site. Program start date not found online. Low yearbook relevance (adult program, no yearbook series expected).

name: Normandy High School - Eden Seminary Campus
district_operator: Normandy School District / Normandy Schools Collaborative
notes: This row is a BUILDING-level row: the school is the same continuous Normandy High School that still operates at 6701 St. Charles Rock Rd. Per the SHSMO Normandy School District Collection finding aid (S0326) and the district's own history page: voters authorized a $200,000 bond to buy the former Eden Theological Seminary property (corner of Lucas & Hunt and St. Charles Rock Rd) in 1922/1924 (sources conflict on bond date); the school opened for the 1923-24 year sharing the campus with Eden students, ~300 students, 13 teachers. Wikipedia's NSC school list gives 'Normandy High School - 1925'; opening year given as 1923 here (first year of operation). A 1949 fire burned most of the ornate four-story seminary building; classes ran split-session 1949-50; the surviving first floor was demolished in 1958 and replaced by Central Hall (completed ~1959). 'Closed 1958' therefore refers only to the original building. The continuing school is tracked separately in batch10 (ALL-328 'Normandy High School'; ALL-329 'Normandy High School - Historical Campus' is probably this same campus) -- flagged as cross-batch overlap, not merged. Actual ZIP is 63133 (Wellston), not 63121.

name: Normandy High School - Original High School Classes
notes: SHSMO S0326 finding aid: first Normandy high-school classes were taught at the old Washington School building in 1907; the first class (four students) graduated in 1911; the school could not meet accreditation requirements and closed in spring 1912. Wikipedia's Normandy HS article says 'closed in 1911' -- the 1911/1912 discrepancy noted; SHSMO's 'spring 1912' used. Wikipedia's NSC school list names this entity 'Washington High School - 1907'. The district had NO high school 1912-1923 (students tuitioned to neighboring districts), so ALL-339 is the eventual successor rather than a direct absorption. Per the Wikipedia Normandy HS article, an even earlier ~1-year high-school attempt operated at Lincoln Elementary in Pagedale before this.

name: Normandy Junior High School - Natural Bridge Campus
district_operator: Normandy School District / Normandy Schools Collaborative
notes: SHSMO S0326: the district bought 30 acres on Natural Bridge Rd from the Sisters of the Cenacle in 1947 and began construction in 1948; the 1949 seminary fire forced split-session classes in 1949-50 while the junior high was finished -- so 'opened 1949' may mean construction completion vs. full occupancy ~1950. Wikipedia's NSC school list dates it 1949. The building later operated as Normandy Middle School and then the 'Normandy 7th-8th Grade Center', which closed for the 2019-20 school year when NSC moved to the EleMiddle (grades 1-8) model per the fall 2018 district newsletter and Prop N documentation. The middle-school program continues as 'Normandy Middle School at Lucas Crossing', 7837 Natural Bridge Rd (no seed row -- successor left unknown). The 7855 Natural Bridge building is now the Normandy Early Learning Center (PS-K), still in district use. OVERLAP FLAG: batch10 row ALL-330 'Normandy Junior High School' is almost certainly the same entity -- kept separate per no-merge rule.

name: Washington School
notes: First school of the Normandy district (District No. 2, Township 46, Range 6 East, Eden, St. Louis County): built 1894 on one acre in the northeast corner of what is now Valhalla Cemetery, per the district history cited in Wikipedia's NSC article. SHSMO S0326 says three elementary schools including Washington were already operating when the district formalized July 12, 1894, and that a NEW Washington School building was constructed in 1895 -- so this original building was replaced after only ~1 year (whether it was demolished or continued in auxiliary use is not stated; closed_year 1895 is probable, not confirmed). Seed's 'closed 1930' appears to treat the whole site lineage through the 1930 move; recorded per building here. Old Washington also hosted the district's first high-school classes 1907-1912 (see ALL-340). Successor building = ALL-345; the same school lineage continues today as Washington Elementary (ALL-346).

name: Washington School - 1895 Building
notes: Replacement building for the original 1894 Washington School (ALL-344), built 1895 per SHSMO S0326. Operated until the district opened the 1930 Washington School building at 1730 N Hanley Rd (ALL-346, 'began operations in 1930' per Wikipedia's NSC article, which also lists 'Washington School - 1930'). Rows ALL-344/345/346 are one continuous school in three buildings; kept separate per seed structure. Building-level closure (1930) is probable -- exact year the 1895 structure stopped serving students is inferred from the successor's opening.

name: Washington School - 1930 Building
district_operator: Normandy School District / Normandy Schools Collaborative
notes: Still operating as Washington Elementary School, 1730 N Hanley Rd, on the current NSC enrollment list (grades 1-5 EleMiddle). Wikipedia's NSC article confirms it 'began operations in 1930' and locates it in Vinita Park. Received Prop N additions (STEAM studio, new entryway) in 2019. Actual ZIP is 63114 per the district's own address list; seed's 63121 reflects the community served. Successor to the 1894/1895 Washington buildings (ALL-344, ALL-345).

name: Normandy School
notes: One of the district's three original schools (operating when the district formalized July 12, 1894); the surviving building at 7629 Natural Bridge Rd was built 1897 per SHSMO S0326. The school itself likely predates 1894 -- founding year unknown. Seed notes (via a Missouri historic survey) say the 1897 building was later used as Roosevelt School, so 'closed' here means renamed to Roosevelt (ALL-348); the rename year (~1930 per seed) is uncertain -- Wikipedia's NSC school list instead gives the Roosevelt span as '1897-1938', which would imply the building was always called Roosevelt. The two sources conflict and the true rename date needs the underlying historic survey. SITE STATUS FLAG: the address is now Murchison Tabernacle CME Church (confirmed, thirddistrictcme.org), but builtstlouis.net describes the present church structure as '1960s vintage' -- so the 1897 school building was probably demolished/replaced on the site rather than surviving as the seed implies. ALL-347 and ALL-348 are arguably the same continuous school; kept separate per no-merge rule.

name: Roosevelt School
notes: Same physical building as ALL-347 (7629 Natural Bridge Rd, built 1897) under the Roosevelt name. Wikipedia's NSC school list gives 'Roosevelt School - 1897-1938' (probably the building's lifespan); the seed gives 1930-1938, consistent with a ~1930 rename of Normandy School. Both sources agree the Roosevelt name ended in 1938. Why it closed and where students went is not documented online -- successor left unknown; recommend the underlying Missouri historic survey / district board minutes for a human follow-up. Site is now Murchison Tabernacle CME Church (1960s-vintage building per builtstlouis.net).

name: Lincoln School
notes: Established ~1900 (Wikipedia NSC list: 'Lincoln School - est. 1900'; SHSMO S0326 puts Lincoln among the elementaries added in the first decade of the 1900s). In Pagedale at 6815 Robbins Ave. Notable: per the Normandy High School Wikipedia article, the district ran a very early (~1-year) high-school program inside Lincoln Elementary before the 1907 Washington School attempt. Wikipedia's NSC article states Lucas Crossing Elementary School (scheduled to open 2001) took students formerly at Lincoln Elementary -- closed ~2001 with Lucas Crossing as successor (no seed row, id left unknown).

name: Garfield School
district_operator: Normandy School District / Normandy Schools Collaborative
notes: Established 1906 per the NSC school list (SHSMO S0326 likewise places Garfield among the 1900s-decade additions). At 6506 Wright Way, Pine Lawn. Per Wikipedia's NSC article, Barack Obama School is 'a consolidation of Garfield Elementary School and Pine Lawn Elementary School'; the board voted to name it in 2010 and it began operations in 2011 -- closed year recorded as 2011 (the consolidation year may be 2010 or 2011 depending on whether one counts the vote or the opening). Successor = Barack Obama Elementary (batch12 row ALL-357). Seed's Beyond Housing association not independently verified.

name: McKinley School
notes: Wikipedia's NSC school list gives 'McKinley School - 1907'; the seed's 1906 ('established 1906-07') is within rounding -- recorded as 1907. Wikipedia locates McKinley Elementary in Velda City with a Hillsdale postal address (seed's 2100-2132 Lucas & Hunt Rd is consistent with the Lucas & Hunt corridor through Velda City). Lucas Crossing Elementary (scheduled to open 2001) took students formerly at McKinley -- closed ~2001; successor Lucas Crossing Elementary has no seed row (id unknown).

name: Harrison School
notes: Established 1907 per the NSC school list (SHSMO S0326 confirms Harrison among the early-1900s additions). At 8121 Albin Ave with a Vinita Park postal address per Wikipedia. Seed's historic-survey note that the building was also called 'Wheaton School' not independently verified but plausible (Wheaton is a nearby area name). Lucas Crossing Elementary (scheduled to open 2001) took students formerly at Harrison -- closed ~2001; successor Lucas Crossing Elementary has no seed row (id unknown).

name: Jefferson School
district_operator: Normandy School District / Normandy Schools Collaborative
notes: Opened 1929 per the NSC school list (SHSMO S0326 also lists Jefferson among elementaries added as the district grew). Still operating as Jefferson Elementary, 4315 Cardwell Dr (Pasadena Hills), on the current NSC enrollment list (grades 1-5 EleMiddle); received Prop N additions in 2019 alongside Washington Elementary.
